detailed_rationale: JBM Auto's legacy business is sheet-metal components and tools/dies/moulds for the auto industry, but its growth narrative today is electric buses, where it holds a genuine market-leading 30-35% share and operates what it describes as the largest dedicated integrated EV/e-bus manufacturing ecosystem outside China -- a real structural beneficiary of India's push to electrify public bus fleets (FAME/PM-eBus Sewa-type schemes). Reported growth has been consistently good: Q1 FY27 (Jun 2026) revenue of Rs.1,442cr (+15% YoY) and profit of Rs.44cr (+13% YoY); FY26 revenue Rs.6,088cr (+12%) and profit Rs.238cr (+12%); 5-year profit CAGR of 35.3% (Screener.in). But several balance-sheet and working-capital signals have deteriorated together: debtor days jumped sharply from 82.4 to 131 (a ~59% increase) -- consistent with the well-documented industry issue of slow payments from cash-strapped state transport undertakings that buy e-buses -- while debt rose to Rs.3,029cr (from Rs.2,630cr) and interest expense rose 29% YoY (Rs.318cr vs Rs.247cr), outpacing profit growth. Interest coverage is weak at ~2.1x (no financial-sector exemption applies here -- this is an industrial company). The stock's own balance-sheet flag is AMBER, and it trades at a rich ~73x earnings / ~10x book value.
recommendation_rationale: The quant score flags this as a Sell on the 1-year view. My research corroborates rather than rescues it: the sharp deterioration in debtor days signals real collection stress from e-bus customers, debt and interest costs are rising faster than profit, interest coverage is thin, and the valuation (73x) leaves no room for these working-capital pressures to worsen. I am not rescuing this Sell.
summary: JBM Auto is the market leader in India's fast-growing electric-bus segment, but the latest results show real strain underneath the growth headline -- receivables have stretched sharply, likely reflecting slow payments from public-transport customers, while debt and interest costs are rising faster than profit. At a rich valuation, we agree with the model's Sell signal.
positive_para: JBM Auto has built genuine, hard-to-replicate scale and market leadership in India's electric-bus rollout, a multi-year structural growth category backed by government policy, and has delivered consistent double-digit revenue and profit growth with a strong historical 5-year profit CAGR (35.3%).
negative_para: Debtor days nearly doubling (82.4 to 131) is a serious red flag for a company selling substantially to government/public-transport-linked customers -- it signals real collection risk, not just paper growth -- and this is happening at the same time as rising debt, interest expense growing faster than profit, and interest coverage already thin (~2.1x). None of this is compensated for by the ~73x earnings multiple; if anything, that multiple assumes flawless execution the working-capital trend is already calling into question.
reverse_dcf_judgment: A ~73x earnings multiple (~10x book value) prices in years of continued strong EV-bus-led growth with no missteps. The sharp deterioration in debtor days and the rising interest burden relative to profit growth suggest the cash-conversion reality of this growth is weaker than the income-statement growth rate implies -- this reads as a valuation that has not yet caught up to a genuine, emerging working-capital risk.
